findings.evidence_quote:
Inductive enc_contractible {C : finType} (Z : {RV P -> C}) (target : R)
    : forall {A : finType}, {RV P -> A} -> Prop :=
findings.explanation: The Inductive return-type uses `forall {A : finType}` with an implicit curly-brace binder. This makes the arity invisible at the declaration site: a reader cannot determine without implicit-argument elaboration whether the predicate is indexed by `A` alone or by the pair `(A, X)`. AUTHORITY.md §C001 requires either (1) an explicit binder — `forall (A : finType), {RV P -> A} -> Prop` — or (2) a named arity alias extracted before the declaration. No preceding `Arity:` comment is present to suppress this finding.
findings.fix_sketch:
Option 1 — explicit binder (in-place):
  Inductive enc_contractible {C : finType} (Z : {RV P -> C}) (target : R)
      : forall (A : finType), {RV P -> A} -> Prop :=
    | ec_base : forall (A : finType) (X : {RV P -> A}),
        `H(Z | X) = target -> enc_contractible Z target X.

Option 2 — named arity alias:
  Definition EncContractibleArity :=
    forall (A : finType), {RV P -> A} -> Prop.
  Inductive enc_contractible {C : finType} (Z : {RV P -> C}) (target : R)
      : EncContractibleArity :=
    | ec_base : forall (A : finType) (X : {RV P -> A}),
        `H(Z | X) = target -> enc_contractible Z target X.

Or add a suppressing comment:
  (* Arity: predicate over RV P -> A, parameterised by sink alphabet A. *)
